subject: FinTechX POC - Observability plan and success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: FinTechX POC - Observability plan and success criteria

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — good conversation. As promised, putting together a concise POC plan focused on observability so we can validate performance, reliability, and operational readiness over a 2-week trial. Please review and confirm or call out any changes.

High-level POC goals / success criteria:
- Functional: Redwood hosts the model variant agreed on the call and responds to sample requests provided by FinTechX (same prompt set).
- Performance: p50 latency < 120ms, p95 < 400ms for the production-like prompt set; token throughput meets expected concurrency (TBD).
- Reliability & Errors: error rate < 0.5% (5xx / client errors) and graceful fallbacks triggered correctly if we simulate capacity constraints.
- Observability: FinTechX can see request-level traces and metrics in your monitoring system and validate that cache-hit behavior and model versioning are visible.

POC scope & timeline:
- Duration: 2 weeks (tentative start Mon Sep 20, 2026).
- Week 0 (pre-kickoff): exchange sample prompts, test keys, and monitoring endpoints.
- Week 1: baseline measurements, integrate tracing/logging, iterate on model/config.
- Week 2: load tests, run success criteria checks, wrap-up demo and handoff.

Ownership:
- FinTechX: Alex (technical lead), Priya (product sponsor) — provide sample prompts, traffic profiles, and SSO/monitoring destinations.
- Redwood: Marissa (eng sponsor / project lead), Marcus (solutions engineering / SE owner for observability integration).

Observability checklist (what we will enable and monitor):
- Dashboards: request-level metrics (p50/p95 latency), throughput (reqs/s, tokens/s), error rates by endpoint, cache hit/miss rates, model-version breakdown.
- Tracing: request IDs propagated, end-to-end traces (OpenTelemetry compatible) for each user request.
- Logs: structured request/response logs (JSON) exported to a bucket or forwarded to your logging provider. Include sampling policy for text payloads.
- Alerts / Regression checks: automatic alerts for latency or error regressions, and a scheduled quality check against the reference prompt set.
- Resource metrics: GPU utilization, memory, queue depth, and tail-latency heatmaps.

Attachments: attaching a short "observability-checklist.pdf" and a sample Grafana dashboard JSON that Marcus will follow up on.

Next steps (please reply to confirm):
1) Confirm POC start date (proposed: Mon Sep 20).
2) Confirm recipients for monitoring access (Datadog account/Datadog API key or S3 bucket / floating log forwarder).
3) Kickoff meeting to align integrations: propose Mon Sep 20 10:00 AM PT — does that work?

Thanks,

--
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — this looks good and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifying questions before we lock the schedule: 

1) Tracing: can Redwood export request-level traces directly into our Datadog instance (we use APM), or do we need to pull traces from an S3 sink? We need to be able to link traces to our internal request IDs.
2) Dashboard templates: can you share a sample Grafana/Datadog dashboard we can import? Marcus was on the call; can he provide the JSON?
3) Data retention & redaction: for logs containing customer prompts, what options do we have for redaction or retention limits during the POC?

Confirmed: Sep 20 kickoff looks okay from our side; Priya will confirm the precise time after aligning with infra.

Quick note: we will generate a 10 req/s synthetic load for the load test and share the prompt set + traffic profile by end of day Friday.

Appreciate it — Alex

Alex — quick technical answers and what we'll deliver before kickoff: 

Tracing:
- Redwood supports OpenTelemetry. We can push spans to Datadog APM directly if you provide a write API key and ingest endpoint; alternately we can export traces to an S3 bucket or to Jaeger/OTLP endpoints you host.
- We'll ensure a stable request_id header is propagated (you can supply your app's request_id header name).

Logs:
- We produce structured JSON logs per request (request_id, model_version, prompt_hash, latency_ms, token_count, error_code).
- For PII/redaction: we can apply prompt redaction rules (drop or hash prompt text) and set a retention TTL on logs. We will include a sample redaction config.

Dashboards / Metrics:
- We'll provide a Grafana dashboard JSON (attached: redwood-grafana-dashboard.json) with panels for p50/p95 latency, throughput, error rate, cache hit ratio, tokens/sec, and GPU utilization.
- Metric names we will emit: redwood.requests.latency_ms.{p50,p95}, redwood.requests.errors.count, redwood.requests.throughput.req_s, redwood.cache.hit_ratio, redwood.model.version{tag}.requests.

Sampling & Cost controls:
- Default: 100% sampling for traces during the POC window for full visibility, configurable down to 1% for production.
- We will enable prefix/KV caching and report cache-hit metrics so you can validate savings.

Deliverables before kickoff (Sep 20):
- Sample Grafana JSON + import instructions (attached).
- Observability checklist PDF with steps to wire Datadog/OTLP.
- A short runbook for how to trigger simulated failures for the POC (to exercise fallbacks).

Attachment: redwood-grafana-dashboard.json (Grafana dashboard JSON), observability-checklist.pdf (one-page checklist).

If it helps, proposed kickoff: Mon Sep 20 10:00 AM PT — I can join as SE.
